chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he

said regarding the sexually impure person (junub) who washes (performs ghusl), so drops of water drip from his body into the vessel, and water splashes from the ground and ends up in the vessel: 'There is no problem with this, all of it.'

key_terms.الْإِنَاء: A vessel or container used to hold water for ritual washing
key_terms.الْجُنُب: A person in a state of major ritual impurity (janaba), typically resulting from sexual intercourse or seminal emission, requiring ghusl (full ritual bath) to restore purity
key_terms.لَا بَأْس: A legal formula meaning 'there is no harm/problem', indicating permissibility in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.يَغْتَسِل: To perform ghusl — the mandatory full-body ritual bath to remove the state of major impurity
key_terms.يَنْتَضِح: To splash or spurt back; here referring to water that rebounds from the ground during washing

ai.seo_question: Is water that drips from a junub person's body during ghusl ritually pure according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a ruling permitting the use of water that has been contaminated by droplets falling from the body of a junub (sexually impure person) during ghusl, as well as water that splashes up from the ground during washing. This hadith addresses a common concern during the ritual bath: whether water that drips off the body or rebounds from the ground renders the remaining water in the vessel ritually impure. The Imam's authoritative ruling — 'there is no problem with this, all of it' — resolves this concern by declaring such water permissible for continued use.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Shihaab Bin Abd Rabbih, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the sexually impure man washing, so drops of the water drop off from his body into the vessel, and the water from the ground flows into the vessel: ‘There is no problem with this, all of it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Shihab ibn ‘Abd Rabbihi who has said the following:

“It is about the case of a man who takes Ghusl (bath) and water-drops from his body sprinkle into the water container and from the ground. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
